correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed finite-extension counting: by ultrahomogeneity and universality, a complete ordered injective type is uniquely determined by its labelled internal graph H and adjacency subsets Si^(t) to each of b disjoint named K_r. No K_{r+1} can involve two distinct parameter cliques; hence c_r(H)^b factorization. For a clique C of s tuple coordinates the K_{r+1}-free condition is |intersection Si for i in C|<=r−s. For edgeless, single edge and incident two edges, count admissible local assignments by inclusion–exclusion, obtaining the three B formulas. Disjoint two-edge pattern has strictly smaller base because a>r, and adding ANY further internal edge imposes a strictly new forbidden assignment, proving uniform integer gap >=1; a finite fixed set of labelled H yields O((B2−1)^b). Reconstructed triangle local inclusion-exclusion: 13 allowed patterns on the two coordinates outside each r−2 common core gives B_triangle. New independent complete local-mask enumeration for (r,k)=(3,3),(4,3),(3,4),(4,4) matched every leading base and strict remaining-base order: for (3,3) all four 343,322,304,247; conditional rare-edge convergence follows from strict gap. General proof holds all fixed r,k>=3 and b>=1; finite tests do not imply infinite limits.
